solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: That's right. A box lined with copper

indicators.note: a box lined with something has it inside its walls, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A confirmation that a packing case really does have a copper lining.
explanation.definitionFit: Something correct or exact is described as right; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Agree there is a pronounced aroma

indicators.note: pronounced means the words are spoken, so we want something that sounds like them

parts.note: an aroma is a scent or smell

explanation.surface: Someone confirming that there is a strong smell in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'a scent' is indistinguishable from the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To give consent or concur is to agree; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: New car tax most men just won't wear

indicators.note: new suggests the word car is made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: A complaint about a car tax that nobody is prepared to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear' reads like 'put up with' a tax; it is literal: a neckerchief few men put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a neckerchief, a dated piece of neckwear that few men choose to put on today.

clue.text: Saying little when it turns up in the centrefold

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: the word centre folded over, its last two letters brought round to the front, gives RECENT

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word it is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A glamour model in a magazine's middle pages who turns out to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: TI (it turned up) goes inside RECENT, which is CENTRE folded: its final RE swung round to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticent person is reserved and says little, keeping their thoughts to themselves.

clue.text: W-well returned, which makes a difference

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: the stammered 'W-well' stands for a stammered synonym, well meaning fit, so f-fit

explanation.surface: A stammering speaker conceding that a return made a real difference.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer in 'W-well' tells you to stammer the synonym too: well = FIT, stuttered as FFIT, then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A difference of opinion is a minor quarrel, which is exactly what a tiff is.

clue.text: Confirmed bachelors before the big-eyed sweetie appears

indicators.note: before places the bachelors ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, so bachelors are BAs
confirmed, as in fixed or settled, means set

explanation.surface: Confirmed bachelors appearing ahead of a doe-eyed sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confirmed bachelors' is a stock phrase, but here the words split into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset hound is a short-legged dog with famously droopy, soulful eyes, a lovable pet.

clue.text: A street name? Wrong

parts.note: Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone queries an address and decides the street name is incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: Going astray means going off course or into error, so the word means awry or mistaken.

clue.text: 'The stone is perhaps flawed,' I interposed

indicators.note: interposed means put between, so the letter I is set inside the other letters
flawed suggests something damaged, so the letters of perhaps are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeweller's aside, interjected, that the gem in question might be flawed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I interposed' looks like a speaker's tag after a quotation; it is the instruction to insert I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious blue gemstone, a kind of corundum.

clue.text: Moderate, taking time, the 17th clue

parts.note: with sixteen across clues, the seventeenth clue in the list is the first down clue

explanation.surface: A puzzle note telling the solver to go easy and take their time over clue 17.
explanation.walkthrough: Count the clues: sixteen across come first, so the 17th is the one numbered 1 in the down list.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate something is to soften it or make it less extreme, as in muting a strong colour.

clue.text: There's a light swell when you set sail

parts.note: a star is a light in the sky
a swell is a dandy or posh person, a toff

explanation.surface: Sailors noting a gentle sea swell as the boat departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light swell' reads as a mild wave; it is two pieces, a celestial light and a well-dressed gentleman (TOFF, British slang for a posh person).
explanation.definitionFit: To set sail is to begin a journey, which is to get going or begin.

clue.text: Intervene and set out to fix

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of set are rearranged

parts.note: to pin something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: Instructions to intervene and get something repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: To step in is to get involved in a situation, to interpose oneself.

clue.text: The quiet sound of talk

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a rattle is a sound of things knocking together

explanation.surface: A musing on the hushed noise of conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quiet sound' reads as a soft noise; the words split into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle chatter or babble is talk of a trivial sort, a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Headache is gone, leaving just a trace

indicators.note: gone means departed, so the word is is removed

parts.note: a headache in the sense of an annoyance is a nuisance

explanation.surface: A sufferer whose headache has lifted, with only a faint ache remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle shade or slight difference is a hint, just a trace of something.

clue.text: Whispered about the bad, scruffy exterior

indicators.note: being the exterior means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other
scruffy means untidy, so the letters of the words are jumbled

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone muttered about the villain with a shabby appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruffy' turns THE BAD into BATHED, which as an 'exterior' goes round RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe words is to say them very softly, so the past form means murmured.

clue.text: Having no food, isn't worried. Takes cigarette out

indicators.note: takes ... out means the anagram has the cigarette on its outside
takes ... out means the anagram has the cigarette on its outside, wrapped round it

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette

indicators.note: worried means troubled or disturbed, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone on a diet insists they aren't bothered, and lights up instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns ISNT into STIN, which goes inside FAG (British slang for a cigarette).
explanation.definitionFit: Going without eating is abstaining from food, as in a religious fast.

clue.text: Find key in the urn, rooting about

indicators.note: in places the key within the other letters
rooting about suggests rummaging and stirring things up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: A is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone rummaging in an urn to find a lost key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rooting about' rearranges THE URN to UNERTH, and the key A goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig up or discover something is to find it, the literal sense being to get it out of the ground.

clue.text: Turning to fend, produce a gun

indicators.note: turning means turning round, so the letters of the word are reversed

parts.note: to ward off is to fend off

explanation.surface: Someone spinning round to defend themselves by pulling out a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a weapon is to pull it from its holster or sheath.

clue.text: Third party insurance for two going to court

definitions.text: Third party insurance for two going to court

parts.words: Third party insurance for two going to court
parts.note: a courting couple once had a third person along to guarantee propriety, a kind of insurance

explanation.surface: Reads like motor insurance cover for two people facing a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third party insurance' and 'court' suggest cars and lawsuits; the court is romantic courting.
explanation.definitionFit: An older escort accompanying a young couple courting acts as a third party ensuring proper conduct.

clue.text: Meant as a cue to go into action

indicators.note: go into means enter, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a deed is an action
a cue is a sign or signal to act

explanation.surface: Describes a prompt intended to spur someone to act.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done on purpose or intended was planned, done by design.

clue.text: Happened to drop, having been holding

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to drop is to fall

explanation.surface: Something happened to fall while it was being held.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic or literary for occurred, as in 'what has befallen him?'

clue.text: Incline to follow closely

definitions.meaning: a ship that leans or tilts to one side is said to do this
a dog trained to keep close behind its owner does this on command

explanation.surface: An instruction to lean in and keep close.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautically a ship tilts over, and a dog walks close at its owner's feet on the command for that.

clue.text: At last turn was front runner but broke down

indicators.note: turn means turned about, so the letters of last are rearranged

parts.note: to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: A racehorse leading until the final bend, then failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last turn' looks like the final bend of a race; 'turn' rearranges LAST to STAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that has cut out has failed, broken down.

clue.text: Walk free and set about reforming

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other
reforming means forming anew, so the letters of set are rearranged

parts.note: to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Someone released from prison and getting on with reforming their life.
explanation.definitionFit: A long step is a pace, and to walk with long steps is to stride.

clue.text: Master criminal having a drink

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts
lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A crime boss having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master criminal' is a stock phrase; it splits into two pieces, the second LAG, British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified sweet wine from Spain, named after its port city, is a drink.

clue.text: Having diminished, after a century died out

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation first, the other piece following it

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a century
eased means lessened, diminished

explanation.surface: Something lessened and then disappeared after a hundred years.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop or come to an end is a synonym of dying out.

clue.text: Very eager to put one in the picture

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside another

parts.note: panting means very eager, desperate for something
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone desperate to be informed or included in the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put one in the picture' reads as to inform someone; here it builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An artwork in paint is a picture.

clue.text: A long time on mother's ruin

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece put on another follows it

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Years of drinking gin, the spirit nicknamed mother's ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother's ruin' is British slang for gin; here the phrase splits: DAM, and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To harm or wreck something badly is to ruin it.

clue.text: Lacking backbone, the Colonel lost his head

indicators.note: losing a head means dropping the first letter

parts.note: Colonel Blimp is a cartoon character, a pompous reactionary British officer

explanation.surface: A spineless military officer who panicked.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp, a British cartoon from the 1930s, gives BLIMP; 'lost his head' means panicked but drops the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble or floppy, without firmness or spirit, is weak, lacking backbone.

clue.text: Followed by police, managed to get off

indicators.note: followed by places the other piece after this one

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Someone tailed by police manages to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get off' sounds like escaping; the definition is 'off', meaning gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off is spoiled, sour and stale.

clue.text: 'Girl Guide' in it proves to be a red herring

definitions.text: proves to be a red herring

indicators.note: in it means the guide piece goes inside the girl piece

parts.note: miss is a girl or young woman
to lead is to guide

explanation.surface: A Girl Guide turns up in a story, but she is only a distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl Guide' (the British Girl Scouts) is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a false clue, so proving to be one deceives or puts people off the track.

clue.text: Went through the motions of agreeing

definitions.text: Went through the motions of agreeing

parts.words: Went through the motions of agreeing
parts.note: the motions here are literal head movements that signal yes

explanation.surface: Someone pretending to agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went through the motions' usually means acting half-heartedly; here it is the literal head movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving the head up and down is the gesture for yes.

clue.text: Foreigner gets waters to drain off

parts.note: a spa is a place where people take the waters

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of drain are scrambled

explanation.surface: A visitor from abroad takes the waters, then drains them away.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Spain is a foreigner to a British solver.
